text:
maria: seeing a ton of 502s and retries from the inference svc in eu-west-2, GPU nodes on pool-gpu-a are pegged while others idle. sudden tail latency spike. anyone else?

sam: yea saw alerts. pods in svc-infer are healthy but per-pod qps is very lopsided. seems like e-w routing skew.

jia: digging in — quick outputs:

```
# on node-42
ipvsadm -L -n --stats
TCP  ClusterIP:443 rr
 -> 10.10.5.23:10250 Weight: 100 Conns: 2345
 -> 10.10.6.19:10250 Weight: 1 Conns: 19
 -> 10.10.7.11:10250 Weight: 1 Conns: 12
```

kubectl get endpoints svc-infer -o wide
ENDPOINTS: 10.10.5.23:10250,10.10.6.19:10250,10.10.7.11:10250

maria: whoa weight 100 on one backend? we never set weights like that.

sam: that explains it — IPVS is sending most traffic to 10.10.5.23. can we confirm kube-proxy config?

jia: kube-proxy logs look normal but I see frequent resyncs older nodes + controller churn after the rolling kernel patch two hours ago. log snippet:

```
W0308 10:02:12.123 kube-proxy: service updated, recalculating ipvs rules
I0308 10:02:12.124 kube-proxy: sync ended (changes: endpoints-weight-change)
```

nate: we pushed a NIC firmware + RDMA enablement to pool-gpu-a earlier today to test throughput. could that change arg to IPVS hashing or weight calculation?

sam: RDMA kernel stacks can change skb steering behavior; IPVS weights shouldn't be impacted directly but conntracking/timeouts might. also noticed MTU mismatch warnings on node-42: `dmesg: UDP: short packet, expected 1500 got 1442`

maria: so maybe fragmentation/path-mtu + RDMA offload + kube-proxy resync combined to create biased endpoint selection?

jia: hypothesis: during the resync sequence kube-proxy reinstalled ipvs entries but the endpoint set loader read an ephemeral metric (node 5 reported as healthy but with duplicates) and applied skewed weights. ipvsadm shows weight fields set during sync when non-equal endpoints had different session counts; our kube-proxy variant tries to preserve weights on resync.

sam: quick mitigation: mark the hot backend 10.10.5.23 as unschedulable in svc (kubectl annotate endpoints svc-infer skip-weight-sync=true) — is that a thing?

jia: not a built-in field but we can do `kubectl patch endpoints svc-infer --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/subsets/0/addresses/0/targetRef/uid","value":"stale"}]'` to force resync and equalize weights (ugly).

nate: I'd prefer not to patch endpoints manually. alternative: restart kube-proxy on the nodes with the bad view so they rebuild ipvs fresh. small rolling restart across pool-gpu-a?

maria: yes do that. also revert RDMA firmware on one node to confirm causality.

sam: rolling restart plan: drain kube-proxy daemonset pods one AZ at a time (grace 10s) -> wait 60s -> observe ipvs weights. I'll run a script and coordinate with oncall.

jia: ran `kubectl rollout restart ds/kube-proxy -n kube-system --field-selector spec.nodeName=node-42` on node-42 only, ipvs weights are now uniform: 1,1,1 and connections rebalanced. tail latency dropped back to normal.

maria: nice. that points to resync bug + state preservation. we should open a ticket to patch kube-proxy to avoid preserving stale weights on resync.

nate: opened ticket INFRA-863: "kube-proxy ipvs resync can preserve skewed endpoint weights after controller churn (possible interaction with NIC firmware)" and linked logs.

sam: action items:
- revert RDMA firmware on test nodes (nate)
- run a small canary of kernel/firmware on pool-gpu-b before wider roll (nate)
- add health-check to kube-proxy that zeros ipvs weights on full resync (jia + eng-runtime)
- postmortem if recurrence (maria)

maria: I'll keep the incident open for 4h and monitor. tagging @deploy-bot to block new canary pushes to pool-gpu-a until we finish.

deploy-bot: Deployment gating enabled for node pool: pool-gpu-a — new canaries blocked.

sam: follow-up: add an alert for abrupt endpoint weight divergence (ipvsadm metric > 5x median) so we catch this earlier.

jia: added a Grafana panel and an alert rule (PR #2123).

maria: thanks all. summary: kube-proxy resync + RDMA/MTU changes caused ipvs to end up with skewed weights; rolling kube-proxy fixed it. next: safer firmware rollout and a small kube-proxy fix. :eyes:
